profile.headline: Mohit Lamba builds backend systems, AI agents, and data pipelines that hold up in production.
profile.heroTag: I build the parts of a product most people never see — the pipelines, the agents, the systems that keep running at 3am. Currently obsessed with making AI agents actually reliable in production.
profile.availabilityBadge: AVAILABLE FOR BACKEND · AI ENGINEERING ROLES
profile.availabilityStatus: Open for high-scale backend engineering & AI infrastructure roles
bioParagraphs: I'm a full-stack developer who ended up specializing in the harder half of the stack: backend systems and AI infrastructure. I like problems where the interesting part isn't the UI — it's what happens after the request leaves the browser.

At EY, I helped build an EPFO WhatsApp engagement platform supporting 1M+ active campaign users — the kind of scale where every shortcut you take in the backend eventually finds you. That's where I learned to care about reliability, not just features.

More recently, at Mednex, I helped build an autonomous GTM AI platform now running campaigns for 50+ B2B clients across thousands of leads — agentic orchestration, RAG, and list-building pipelines, not just a thin LLM wrapper.
I design around SOLID principles and layered boundaries — Clean and Hexagonal Architecture — because six months from now, someone (often me) has to change this code without fear.

projects.title: ToolTap
projects.description: A backend-first AI agent that turns WhatsApp into a full tool-calling interface. The interesting part isn't the chat UI — it's the orchestration underneath: async webhook processing, tool-calling loops, and graceful failure when the LLM or a tool times out mid-conversation.

projects.title: Autonomous GTM AI Platform
projects.description: AI-driven go-to-market workflows — ICP generation, list building, market research, and personalized copywriting, running as coordinated agents rather than a single prompt. I worked across both the AI layer and the backend feeding it: agent orchestration, external data providers, and business-context processing.
